concepts.title: Nature of Tertiary Activities
concepts.definition: Tertiary activities involve the provision of services and exchange of produced goods - trade, transport, communication and commercial services; unlike secondary work they do not transform matter but support production and connect producers with consumers.
concepts.key_idea: Services have outgrown manufacturing in developed economies, making the tertiary sector the largest employer of the modern age.

concepts.title: Tourism: The Largest Tertiary Activity
concepts.definition: Tourism has become the world's single largest tertiary activity with about 250 million registered jobs and revenue near 40 per cent of total GDP, fed by cultural, adventure and historical tourism; coastal, mountain and heritage resources drive the flows.
concepts.key_idea: Tourism sustains about 250 million jobs worldwide, its share of world revenue being around 40 per cent of total GDP.

concepts.title: Medical Services and Medical Tourism
concepts.definition: Medical tourism draws foreign patients to countries offering skilled care at lower cost; about 55,000 patients from the USA visited India in 2005 for treatment, showing how services are traded across borders.
concepts.key_idea: When services cross borders, wages and standards arbitrage: skilled doctors and low costs make India a destination, not a source, of patients.
concepts.textbook_ref: legy106.txt medical services for overseas patients (55,000 US patients in 2005)

solution_steps.explain: 55,000 US patients came to India in 2005 for treatment
low cost plus internationally comparable skill draws patients across borders
balancing export care with domestic needs is the policy challenge

concepts.title: Quaternary and Quinary Activities
concepts.definition: Quaternary activities are knowledge-based services - research, information generation, consultancy, data processing and outsourcing - carried by professionals; quinary activities are the highest-level decision-making by top executives and officials.
concepts.key_idea: Outsourcing shifts quaternary tasks to distant countries, making knowledge work as tradable as goods.
concepts.textbook_ref: legy106.txt quaternary-quinary sections and outsourcing discussion

solution_steps.explain: knowledge services are quaternary; top-level executive decisions are quinary
back offices in Bangalore and Manila serve clients in distant time zones
education and digital access decide who participates in this sector
